reforms.description: The government has initiated the creation of special zones where key regulations are abolished or modified on a trial basis to enhance local autonomy and stimulate innovation. This initiative aims to stimulate regulatory competition among municipalities to attract new business activities, including research and development, by allowing local governments to propose reforms for approval.
reforms.growth_orientation_rationale: By enhancing local autonomy and stimulating innovation through regulatory competition, the initiative is expected to raise productivity and attract new business activities.
reforms.status_evidence: The initiative has been actively implemented to stimulate innovation.
reforms.importance_rationale: The reform represents a structural change aimed at enhancing innovation through regulatory modifications.
reforms.source_quote: The special zone initiative has also helped to increase transparency; in many cases, local authorities have asked for the elimination of regulations that do not exist.
reforms.cross_verification_note: The initiative aims to stimulate innovation and allows local governments to propose reforms for research and development, indicating a direct connection to innovation instruments.

reforms.description: Japan introduced an investment tax credit for R&D in 2003, allowing firms to deduct R&D expenditures from corporate income tax liability. This indirect support instrument aims to incentivize private-sector research and development investment.
reforms.growth_orientation_rationale: R&D tax credits reduce the effective cost of private R&D investment, incentivizing firms to increase innovation spending and productivity-enhancing research, thereby supporting long-term GDP growth.
reforms.status_evidence: Text states 'Japan introduced an investment tax credit for R&D in 2003', indicating the reform was in force.
reforms.importance_rationale: A significant but narrower reform introducing a new indirect support instrument for private R&D; not a system-wide structural change.
reforms.source_quote: Following the introduction of an investment tax credit for R&D in 2003, the amount of revenue lost by special deductions in the national corporate income tax increased from 0.4 to 1.7 trillion yen (0.3 per cent of GDP).
reforms.cross_verification_note: The introduction of an investment tax credit for R&D directly incentivizes private-sector research and development investment, aligning with the criteria for inclusion.

all_reforms_including_excluded.description: The reduction of capital requirements for new start-ups in 2003 from 3 million yen to only 1 yen contributed to a 10% rise in the number of newly created companies, facilitating entrepreneurship and innovation.
all_reforms_including_excluded.growth_orientation_rationale: Lowering capital requirements encourages entrepreneurship, leading to increased business formation and innovation.
all_reforms_including_excluded.status_evidence: The reduction in capital requirements has been successfully implemented, resulting in a rise in new startups.
all_reforms_including_excluded.importance_rationale: The reform significantly impacts the startup ecosystem by facilitating the creation of new companies.
all_reforms_including_excluded.source_quote: Another important reform was the reduction of the capital requirements for new start-ups in 2003 from 3 million yen (10 million yen for companies that issue stock) to only 1 yen.
all_reforms_including_excluded.cross_verification_note: The reform focuses on reducing capital requirements for start-ups, which primarily facilitates entrepreneurship rather than directly supporting R&D funding or innovation instruments.

all_reforms_including_excluded.description: Japan established special zones for structural reform in 2002 allowing regulatory experimentation at the local level. Proposals were solicited from local governments, citizens, and enterprises through five rounds of consultation, with accepted proposals implemented either in designated special zones or nation-wide, and an Evaluation Committee assessing outcomes for potential national rollout.
all_reforms_including_excluded.growth_orientation_rationale: While the special zones framework enables regulatory experimentation that could support innovation, the text does not specify innovation-focused outcomes or R&D-related regulatory changes. The growth effect depends on the nature of experiments conducted, which is not detailed.
all_reforms_including_excluded.status_evidence: Text states 'Japan established special zones for structural reform', indicating the reform was in force by 2002.
all_reforms_including_excluded.importance_rationale: A structural, system-wide reform establishing a new governance mechanism for regulatory experimentation across Japan, with potential for nation-wide rollout of successful innovations.
all_reforms_including_excluded.source_quote: The creation of special zones is based on a mix of local initiative, informal consultations, and central government approval... Thus far, there have been five rounds, each lasting around a month, resulting in more than 2300 reform proposals from nearly 1500 entities.
all_reforms_including_excluded.cross_verification_note: The description focuses on regulatory experimentation and structural reform without a clear emphasis on R&D funding or innovation instruments.
